raw_response:
I will still do it close to how I handled it in recent years, because 10.9 mu is not big enough for me to gamble. I have done this 30 years, and at my age I look first at what gave me a steady harvest last year, then I adjust a little for cost and water. Since I have well irrigation, I will lean on wheat and summer maize for the main land, because that is the safest money here. Cotton I will keep on a smaller piece, because it can make money if the price is alright, but it needs more watching and more sprays. With my schooling level, I do look at input labels and I do listen to the dealer and what nearby farmers are doing, but I still trust what I saw in fields around me. For wheat, I will not cut fertilizer too hard, because weak wheat in spring is hard to fix later. I will put enough base fertilizer, water it about 3 times if the season is normal, and aim for around 500 kg per mu. For summer maize after wheat, I will use hybrid seed, keep fertilizer fairly strong, and give 2 irrigations if rain is not enough, because maize here can lose yield very fast if it catches drought at tasseling. For cotton, I will keep the area smaller, use improved seed, give more potash than wheat, and be ready for more pesticide rounds, because cotton without timely control is easy to lose. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than watch yield fall.
